title: Mission: Yozakura Family
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Taiyo Asano, a shy high schooler who lost his family in a car crash, learns that his childhood friend Mutsumi heads a clan of elite spies. To shield him under the family rule of no killing among kin, he marries her and trains as a spy to protect her, against her overprotective brother Kyoichiro and rival organizations such as Tanpopo.
life_message: It holds up a life of loyal, protective love inside a close family, earned through hard training and courage.

content.note: Assassinations, shootings, bombings and torture; Kyoichiro will kill to protect Mutsumi (Wikipedia; AniList Assassins, Swordplay tags).
Tanpopo runs deadly experiments; family members in mortal danger, softened by comedy (Wikipedia).
Teen arranged marriage at the center; a comedic bathing scene with nudity and secret photos of Mutsumi (Wikipedia).
Villains use the power drug Hazakura at a cost; Nanao makes medicines and poisons (Wikipedia).
Taiyo's grief and isolation after losing his family is the starting point (Wikipedia).
Spy tricks, stalking-style overprotection by Kyoichiro played for laughs (to verify).
Weekly Shonen Jump hit with anime, light novels and merchandise (Wikipedia).

dominant: Communitarianism (family loyalty), Traditionalism, Classical virtue ethics

delivery.evidence: AniList summary frames family loyalty through spy-comedy plot; no review on delivery found (to verify).
delivery.note: Family loyalty is carried by action and comedy; how fully rival organizations' views are shown is unverified.

winners_losers: The Yozakura family and Taiyo win by sticking together; outside organizations like Tanpopo that exploit people with drugs and experiments lose. Family loyalty above outside law gets the sympathy.
